findings.issue_text: Anonymous auth is now synchronously coupled to device-tagging DB writes: TagDevice previously ran in a fire-and-forget goroutine with context.Background() and a 2-minute timeout, but now runs inline in Authenticate under the request context with no deadline, so a slow or contended database directly stalls anonymous page loads with no time cap during cache misses or DB degradation (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44, impl.go:147)
The removed recover() means a panic during device tagging now propagates into the auth handler instead of being contained

TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice: the CountDevices check and the insert run in separate statements/sessions with no transaction or row locking, so under burst load N concurrent first-time devices all observe count < limit and all insert, allowing the device count to exceed the configured limit (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:109-117)

updateDevice's WithDbSession callback is not retry-safe: `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` reassigns the captured args slice inside the callback, so on a lock/deadlock retry the query string is prepended a second time, producing 7 bind arguments for 6 ? placeholders and causing Exec to fail with an argument-count error (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:84)

rowsAffected == 0 conflates a no-op update with limit reached on MySQL: go-sql-driver/mysql reports changed rows rather than matched rows, and with second-precision timestamp columns a re-tag of an existing active device within the same second with identical IP/UA is a no-op, so RowsAffected() returns 0 and the store spuriously returns ErrDeviceLimitReached (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95)

Limit rejection surfaces as a raw internal error: Authenticate returns the bare fmt.Errorf("device limit reached") sentinel which flows through the generic authn error path, giving unauthenticated clients a 500 with the raw message instead of a deliberate 4xx (403/429), polluting 5xx error-rate monitoring and making the configured limit-reached condition indistinguishable from a real internal failure (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:45-47)

Verify CountDevices signature: the call site passes time.Time values while sibling ListDevices in the same AnonStore interface takes *time.Time pointers (api.go:73); if CountDevices is declared with *time.Time params the call does not compile and the whole package fails to build (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110)

Device limit enforcement is not atomic (TOCTOU race): the CountDevices limit check and the subsequent insert/upsert in CreateOrUpdateDevice (database.go:76-88) run in separate DB sessions with no transaction, row locking, or constraint, so concurrent requests (or multiple Grafana instances behind an LB, each with its own localCache) can both read count == limit-1, pass the check, and insert, pushing the device count past the configured cap

TagDevice is now called synchronously on the request context inside Authenticate (client.go:44-49, impl.go:144-146) instead of in a detached goroutine, so every cache-miss device tag performs a blocking DB write on the auth critical path; a slow or degraded database now stalls all anonymous traffic even with the default device_limit = 0

DoS amplification when the limit is enabled: each unique device triggers a synchronous COUNT over the 30-day anon_device window before the write, and since anonymous endpoints are unauthenticated with a client-supplied/omittable device identifier, clearing cookies yields a new device per request (bypassing the per-instance localCache), turning one cheap HTTP request into a windowed COUNT plus a write attempt — a full table scan per request if updated_at isn't indexed on anon_device
The 2-minute timeoutTag cap on device tagging was removed; the operation is now bounded only by the request context

MySQL RowsAffected semantics can produce a false ErrDeviceLimitReached for valid existing devices: without clientFoundRows in the DSN, UPDATE reports changed rows rather than matched rows, so a device row that is matched but has identical values (same client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at at the column's timestamp resolution) returns RowsAffected() == 0 and is rejected as limit-reached (database.go:100-106)

Panic isolation around device tagging was removed: the deleted recover() guard ('Tag anon session panic') in client.go:41-49 is gone, so a panic in TagDevice/tagDeviceUI now propagates into the authn flow and fails the request instead of being fully isolated

Anonymous auth hot path now performs synchronous DB I/O with no timeout: device tagging moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (with 2-minute timeout and panic recovery) to a synchronous TagDevice call on the request context, so every local-cache miss adds 1-2 DB round trips inline in authentication, a slow or pool-exhausted DB stalls anonymous auth indefinitely, and client disconnects cancel the tagging write

Provider signature changes with no DI/wire updates in the diff: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService and ProvideAnonDBStore (now requiring a bare int64) changed signatures but no wire.go/wire_gen.go changes appear in the PR, so the code may not compile and wire cannot satisfy the new int64 device limit parameter without a dedicated provider for cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit

COUNT is executed on every tag attempt when the limit is enabled: CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices over the 30-day window before checking whether the device already exists, adding an O(rows in window) aggregate query per cache miss that becomes a full table scan per request if anon_device has no index on the time column

Rejected devices are not negatively cached, causing DB amplification exactly at capacity: the local cache entry is only written after a successful store call, so when ErrDeviceLimitReached occurs nothing memoizes the rejection and every subsequent request from that device repeats both COUNT and UPDATE queries, turning the limiter into a load amplifier in the overload state it exists to protect against

Count-then-insert limit check is not atomic, making the limit only advisory under burst: the SELECT COUNT(*) is followed by a separate INSERT/UPDATE with no transaction, lock, or constraint coupling them, so N concurrent requests can all observe count < limit and all insert, overshooting the cap by the full concurrency level

Returning devices with stale rows are hard-blocked at capacity: updateDevice only matches rows with updated_at within 30 days of the incoming device's timestamp, so a device whose row exists but was last updated 30-61 days ago matches 0 rows and gets ErrDeviceLimitReached/auth failure even though it doesn't count toward the limit, conflating 'stale row' with 'limit reached'

ListDevices materializes the entire 30-day window without pagination (pre-existing): the admin endpoint loads every anon device in the window into memory and serializes it with no LIMIT/pagination, remaining unbounded when the device limit is unset

New anonymous-auth rejection path has no defined HTTP contract: `Authenticate` returns the raw store sentinel `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` directly out of the authn client, so the HTTP status/body for limit-reached failures on every anonymous endpoint is unspecified — no deliberate 429/403, no error code, no API docs, and the error string may leak verbatim through generic error mapping

MySQL affected-rows semantics can spuriously reject already-registered devices: `updateDevice` interprets `rowsAffected == 0` as 'device limit reached', but MySQL (go-sql-driver without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS) reports rows changed rather than matched, so a no-op UPDATE on an existing in-window device (identical client_ip/user_agent, `updated_at` truncating to the same stored value) returns 0 rows and fails auth

Injected `AnonStore` interface replaced with a hard-coded concrete store: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now takes `db.DB` and constructs `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` internally (also used by the admin API), silently bypassing any alternative `AnonStore` implementation previously supplied through the DI graph (enterprise wire bindings, DI-level test fakes) with no compile or runtime error

`ProvideAnonDBStore` exported signature changed without caller/wire consideration: the constructor gained a required `deviceLimit int64` parameter, breaking every out-of-diff caller (enterprise code, other wire registrations, external tests) at compile time, and wire cannot synthesize a binding for the primitive `int64`

Anonymous auth made synchronous: `TagDevice` now runs inline in `Authenticate` on the request context, removing the background goroutine, 2-minute timeout, and panic `recover()` — tagging DB work is now on the anonymous request's critical path, client disconnects cancel tagging so devices can go unrecorded, panics in TagDevice now fail the request as a 500, and TagDevice changed from best-effort (logged, returned nil) to error-propagating for other callers

Device-limit enforcement is racy: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then inserts/updates in separate, non-transactional steps with no unique constraint or locking, so concurrent requests at the boundary all observe `count < limit` and all insert, exceeding the configured cap by roughly the concurrency factor

Required field added to the public `GrafanaConfig` interface with type drift vs. the backend: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` is a required (non-optional) property on the exported `@grafana/data` interface, breaking downstream implementers/mocks at compile time, while the backend declares it as plain `int64` with no `omitempty` so the JSON always contains a number — the `undefined` arm only ever occurs against older backends

Device-limit check in CreateOrUpdateDevice (database.go) is a non-atomic count-then-insert TOCTOU race: CountDevices runs in one DB session and the INSERT happens in a separate WithDbSession transaction with no transaction, row lock, or atomic 'insert only if count < limit' construct, so concurrent requests can all observe count == limit-1 and all insert, overshooting the limit under load

Anonymous auth now blocks synchronously on the DB with no timeout: TagDevice is called synchronously on the request context (client.go) and the previous background goroutine with a 2-minute context timeout and recover() was removed, so DB slowness or pool exhaustion can hang anonymous requests indefinitely, pile up request goroutines, and cascade pool pressure to authenticated traffic

No negative caching for rejected devices: the local cache entry is only set after a successful CreateOrUpdateDevice, so an over-limit device re-executes the full path (CountDevices range scan plus a doomed UPDATE) synchronously on every request, creating a load-amplification/DoS vector; known devices on cache expiry also pay 2 queries instead of 1 upsert when the limit is enabled

updateDevice misinterprets RowsAffected() == 0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached: on MySQL (go-sql-driver defaults to changed rows, not matched rows, unless clientFoundRows is set), a value-identical UPDATE such as two tags of the same device within the same timestamp precision reports 0 affected rows, causing spurious 401 auth failures for legitimate already-registered devices; the same conflation fires if the row is deleted concurrently between the COUNT and the UPDATE

Core success path of the feature is untested: no test verifies that an existing device with updated_at inside the window is still updatable when the limit is reached (updateDevice affecting exactly 1 row and returning nil); a regression in the updated_at BETWEEN bounds would lock out every existing device while the suite stays green

Anonymous.Authenticate behavioral change has zero test coverage: auth changed from a fire-and-forget goroutine (own 2-min timeout + recover()) to a synchronous TagDevice whose ErrDeviceLimitReached fails the entire authentication; no test verifies new device rejection at auth, existing device success, that non-limit TagDevice errors are logged but do not fail auth, the resulting HTTP status (raw error likely mapped to 500), or the removed panic recovery

Config-to-store wiring is never exercised through the service: both service tests build the service with setting.NewCfg() (limit = 0), so the cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit to anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore wiring and the new return err in TagDevice are never hit at the service level; if the ini key or wiring regressed, every test still passes

Count-then-act race in CreateOrUpdateDevice allows exceeding the limit: CountDevices and the insert/update run with no transaction or locking between them, so two concurrent first-time devices can both observe count < limit and both insert, overshooting the cap; no test demonstrates or guards behavior under concurrent requests

30-day window semantics of the limit are untested: no test covers that a device whose last update is >30 days old does not consume limit capacity (allowing a new device to be created), or that an existing-but-expired device whose updateDevice hits 0 rows gets ErrDeviceLimitReached (treated as new)
No test for device_limit ini parsing: no test in pkg/setting asserts the key is read from [auth.anonymous], nor that an invalid value silently disables the feature via MustInt64 falling back to 0

No test that frontend settings expose the new field, and the TS contract doesn't match the backend: AnonymousDeviceLimit is always serialized (no omitempty, always a number) while the TS type is number | undefined, so the undefined case the TS type promises can never occur; no frontendsettings test asserts the value flows from cfg to the response

New limit test doesn't assert resulting store state: after the expected ErrDeviceLimitReached, the test never calls ListDevices to assert exactly one row exists and that the rejected device was not created or partially written, so a regression where the failure path still mutates state would pass unnoticed

Wire/DI graph not updated: ProvideAnonDBStore and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signatures changed but the diff contains no wire set or wire_gen.go changes, so the checked-in wire_gen.go still calls both providers with the old signatures and cannot compile; wire codegen would also fail because nothing can provide a bare int64, and hard-coding anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore inside the service constructor destroys the injectable AnonStore abstraction, breaking any other wire consumer of anonstore.AnonStore

TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice (database.go:102-109): a non-transactional CountDevices followed by INSERT/UPDATE with no transaction, isolation level, advisory lock, or constraint lets concurrent first-seen devices all observe count < limit and all insert, overshooting the configured device limit — an adversarial client can deliberately race past the cap
Device limit check fails open: any error from CountDevices/updateDevice other than the sentinel is swallowed upstream and auth proceeds, so the limit is unenforced exactly when the DB is degraded

No negative caching for rejected devices: only successful tags populate localCache, so a device rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached re-runs CountDevices — an updated_at range query with no index or migration added — plus a doomed UPDATE on every single request, converting over-limit floods into repeated table scans and making the guard a DB-load amplifier / self-inflicted DoS vector

Anonymous auth now synchronously blocks on DB tagging: the fire-and-forget goroutine on context.Background() with its 2-minute timeout was removed, so TagDevice runs inline in Authenticate for every cache-miss request even when device_limit=0, adding DB latency to anonymous request latency with no timeout bound — a slow or hung DB stalls anonymous auth, turning a tracking side-effect into an availability dependency for all anonymous viewers

MySQL changed-rows semantics can reject legitimate, already-registered devices: updateDevice interprets RowsAffected()==0 as device limit reached, but go-sql-driver's default (without clientFoundRows=true in the DSN) reports rows changed rather than matched, so an existing active device with unchanged client_ip/user_agent and same-second updated_at matches the WHERE clause but changes nothing, yielding a spurious ErrDeviceLimitReached and locking out a valid device; needs verification against the MySQL DSN and a MySQL integration test

Device-limit exhaustion is a cheap, long-lived lockout: device identity is client-side-derived (cookie / IP+UA), so an attacker can mint unlimited unique device identities and fill every configured slot, after which every new legitimate anonymous device is hard-rejected for up to 30 days (slots only free on 30-day idle or login-triggered untag), with no per-source rate limiting, slot eviction, or challenge to mitigate it

Over-limit clients receive opaque 500s: returning the raw ErrDeviceLimitReached makes the authn chain treat it as a hard internal error rather than ErrContextAwareClientNotAuthenticated, so affected devices get generic internal-server errors indistinguishable from an outage in error-rate metrics and alerting, giving operators no signal that the configured limit is full — a dedicated error mapping/response is needed

errors.Is sentinel matching is fragile: a %v wrap instead of %w anywhere in an intermediate layer would silently turn the device limit into a no-op (auth proceeds, logged as a warning) — worth guarding with a test

goldens.comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TagDevice was changed from an async, fire-and-forget goroutine using context.Background() with a 2-minute timeout (removed `timeoutTag` and the goroutine in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`) to an inline call `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` under the request context with no explicit deadline. Also, `TagDevice` now returns the UI tagging error (`impl.go` adds `return err`), making DB/write-path errors and latency directly impact authentication/request handling. This is a concrete performance/availability coupling concern grounded in the diff, but not an inherent correctness defect by itself (could be intentional to enforce device limits).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The removed recover() means a panic during device tagging now propagates into the auth handler instead of being contained

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go, Authenticate() used to tag the device in a separate goroutine wrapped with a defer recover(), so any panic inside TagDevice was contained and only logged. The diff removes that goroutine and recover block and calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously without recovery. If TagDevice (or its dependencies) panics, it would now unwind through the auth handler path rather than being contained. This is a robustness/regression risk grounded in the diff, even if no specific panic source is shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Device limit enforcement is not atomic (TOCTOU race): the CountDevices limit check and the subsequent insert/upsert in CreateOrUpdateDevice (database.go:76-88) run in separate DB sessions with no transaction, row locking, or constraint, so concurrent requests (or multiple Grafana instances behind an LB, each with its own localCache) can both read count == limit-1, pass the check, and insert, pushing the device count past the configured cap

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` the limit check does `CountDevices(...)` and, if below the limit, proceeds to create/upsert the device. The count and the subsequent write are not shown to be wrapped in a single transaction or protected by a DB-side constraint/lock. Since `CountDevices` and the later insert/upsert necessarily run as separate statements (and likely separate sessions, as other methods use `WithDbSession`), concurrent requests/instances can both observe `count < limit` and both insert, exceeding `deviceLimit`. Nothing in the diff adds atomic enforcement (e.g., transaction with locking or constraint), so the TOCTOU race described is a real issue exposed by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TagDevice is now called synchronously on the request context inside Authenticate (client.go:44-49, impl.go:144-146) instead of in a detached goroutine, so every cache-miss device tag performs a blocking DB write on the auth critical path; a slow or degraded database now stalls all anonymous traffic even with the default device_limit = 0

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `Authenticate` to call `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously (client.go) instead of launching a detached goroutine with its own timeout/background context. `TagDevice` can return errors from `tagDeviceUI` now (`return err` added in impl.go), and on a cache miss it ultimately persists via the anon store (DB). That means the auth request path can now block on DB work (and potentially be slowed by DB degradation) even when `AnonymousDeviceLimit` is 0 (no limit), though the impact is mitigated by the service’s local cache (impl.go uses `localcache.New(...)`) so it’s not literally every request. This is a concrete performance/availability regression risk rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DoS amplification when the limit is enabled: each unique device triggers a synchronous COUNT over the 30-day anon_device window before the write, and since anonymous endpoints are unauthenticated with a client-supplied/omittable device identifier, clearing cookies yields a new device per request (bypassing the per-instance localCache), turning one cheap HTTP request into a windowed COUNT plus a write attempt — a full table scan per request if updated_at isn't indexed on anon_device

adjudication.rationale: With `AnonymousDeviceLimit > 0`, `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` performs `CountDevices(...)` over a 30-day window on *every* tag attempt before deciding to insert/update (see `if s.deviceLimit > 0 { count, err := s.CountDevices(...); ... }`). In the same diff, anonymous device tagging is made synchronous in `Anonymous.Authenticate` (removed the background goroutine/timeout and now directly calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)`), so each anonymous request can trigger this COUNT. Since the device ID can vary per request (e.g., new/cleared cookies), this can bypass the per-device local cache and turn cheap unauthenticated requests into repeated DB COUNTs + write attempts. Whether the COUNT is a full table scan depends on indexing not shown here, but the amplification vector (COUNT-per-request in an unauth path) is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 2-minute timeoutTag cap on device tagging was removed; the operation is now bounded only by the request context

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go removes the `timeoutTag = 2 * time.Minute` constant and the goroutine that wrapped tagging in `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeoutTag)`. Tagging is now executed synchronously as `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, ...)`, so it is bounded only by the passed-in request context (and can potentially block authentication if that context has no deadline). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change, but not inherently a correctness defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MySQL RowsAffected semantics can produce a false ErrDeviceLimitReached for valid existing devices: without clientFoundRows in the DSN, UPDATE reports changed rows rather than matched rows, so a device row that is matched but has identical values (same client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at at the column's timestamp resolution) returns RowsAffected() == 0 and is rejected as limit-reached (database.go:100-106)

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` (database.go), the code interprets `rowsAffected == 0` from an `UPDATE` as “no matching device” and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. However, the `UPDATE anon_device SET client_ip=?, user_agent=?, updated_at=? ...` can legitimately affect 0 rows even when a row *matches*, if the new values are identical to existing ones (a known MySQL behavior without `clientFoundRows`, where RowsAffected reports changed rows, not matched rows). Since `CreateOrUpdateDevice` uses this path when `count >= s.deviceLimit`, this can incorrectly reject an existing device as limit-reached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Panic isolation around device tagging was removed: the deleted recover() guard ('Tag anon session panic') in client.go:41-49 is gone, so a panic in TagDevice/tagDeviceUI now propagates into the authn flow and fails the request instead of being fully isolated

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the panic-isolating goroutine + recover() block in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go was removed, and TagDevice is now called synchronously (`if err := a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)`) with no recover wrapper. That means any panic inside TagDevice/tagDeviceUI would now propagate through the authn Authenticate call path rather than being contained/logged. However, the diff does not prove a panic can actually occur in TagDevice; it only removes a defensive guard, making this a resilience/robustness concern rather than a demonstrable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anonymous auth hot path now performs synchronous DB I/O with no timeout: device tagging moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (with 2-minute timeout and panic recovery) to a synchronous TagDevice call on the request context, so every local-cache miss adds 1-2 DB round trips inline in authentication, a slow or pool-exhausted DB stalls anonymous auth indefinitely, and client disconnects cancel the tagging write

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Anonymous.Authenticate` changed from spawning a goroutine with `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)` and panic recovery to calling `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously (see `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`, removal of `timeoutTag` and the `go func(){...}` block). `TagDevice` can execute DB I/O via `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(...).CreateOrUpdateDevice` (now also potentially does a `CountDevices` then an `UPDATE`/`INSERT`), so this is now on the auth hot path without an explicit timeout and is tied to the request context (client disconnect/cancellation can abort the write). This is a concrete performance/availability/architecture concern introduced by the change, but not a provable functional defect solely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: COUNT is executed on every tag attempt when the limit is enabled: CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices over the 30-day window before checking whether the device already exists, adding an O(rows in window) aggregate query per cache miss that becomes a full table scan per request if anon_device has no index on the time column

The claim that it is a "full table scan" depends on DB indexing not shown in the diff, so that part isn’t verifiable here, but the added per-request COUNT is directly supported by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rejected devices are not negatively cached, causing DB amplification exactly at capacity: the local cache entry is only written after a successful store call, so when ErrDeviceLimitReached occurs nothing memoizes the rejection and every subsequent request from that device repeats both COUNT and UPDATE queries, turning the limiter into a load amplifier in the overload state it exists to protect against

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new device limit path in `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` that can execute a COUNT and then an UPDATE returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but it does not show how `AnonDeviceService`’s `localCache` is populated or whether failures are cached. adjudication_records.issue_text: Count-then-insert limit check is not atomic, making the limit only advisory under burst: the SELECT COUNT(*) is followed by a separate INSERT/UPDATE with no transaction, lock, or constraint coupling them, so N concurrent requests can all observe count < limit and all insert, overshooting the cap by the full concurrency level

Under concurrent requests, multiple goroutines can all observe `count < s.deviceLimit` and all insert new devices, exceeding the configured cap. The diff shows no atomic mechanism (e.g., single transaction with locking, unique/partial constraint, or conditional insert) to prevent overshoot.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Returning devices with stale rows are hard-blocked at capacity: updateDevice only matches rows with updated_at within 30 days of the incoming device's timestamp, so a device whose row exists but was last updated 30-61 days ago matches 0 rows and gets ErrDeviceLimitReached/auth failure even though it doesn't count toward the limit, conflating 'stale row' with 'limit reached'

adjudication_records.issue_text: New anonymous-auth rejection path has no defined HTTP contract: `Authenticate` returns the raw store sentinel `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` directly out of the authn client, so the HTTP status/body for limit-reached failures on every anonymous endpoint is unspecified — no deliberate 429/403, no error code, no API docs, and the error string may leak verbatim through generic error mapping

With MySQL’s default affected-rows semantics (changed rows, not matched rows), an UPDATE that matches an existing in-window `device_id` but results in no actual column changes can legitimately return 0. In the device-limit path (`CreateOrUpdateDevice` when `count >= s.deviceLimit`), this would incorrectly reject an already-registered device (auth failure) even though the row exists and is within the allowed time window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Device-limit enforcement is racy: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then inserts/updates in separate, non-transactional steps with no unique constraint or locking, so concurrent requests at the boundary all observe `count < limit` and all insert, exceeding the configured cap by roughly the concurrency factor

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), limit enforcement does `CountDevices(...)` and, if `count < s.deviceLimit`, proceeds to the normal upsert/insert path. adjudication_records.issue_text: Required field added to the public `GrafanaConfig` interface with type drift vs. the backend: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` is a required (non-optional) property on the exported `@grafana/data` interface, breaking downstream implementers/mocks at compile time, while the backend declares it as plain `int64` with no `omitempty` so the JSON always contains a number — the `undefined` arm only ever occurs against older backends

Because it is not marked optional (`?`), it becomes a required property for all downstream `GrafanaConfig` implementers/mocks and can cause TypeScript compile breaks. adjudication_records.issue_text: Device-limit check in CreateOrUpdateDevice (database.go) is a non-atomic count-then-insert TOCTOU race: CountDevices runs in one DB session and the INSERT happens in a separate WithDbSession transaction with no transaction, row lock, or atomic 'insert only if count < limit' construct, so concurrent requests can all observe count == limit-1 and all insert, overshooting the limit under load

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (database.go), the new limit enforcement does `CountDevices(...)` first, then (if `count < s.deviceLimit`) proceeds to the normal insert/upsert path in a separate DB operation/session. The diff shows no shared transaction, locking, or atomic SQL constraint tying the count check to the subsequent INSERT/UPSERT, so concurrent requests can all observe `count == limit-1` and each insert, exceeding the configured `deviceLimit`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Anonymous auth now blocks synchronously on the DB with no timeout: TagDevice is called synchronously on the request context (client.go) and the previous background goroutine with a 2-minute context timeout and recover() was removed, so DB slowness or pool exhaustion can hang anonymous requests indefinitely, pile up request goroutines, and cascade pool pressure to authenticated traffic

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a concrete behavioral change: `Anonymous.Authenticate` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` removed the background goroutine + `context.WithTimeout(..., 2*time.Minute)` + `recover()` wrapper, and now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously on the request path. That means auth requests will now wait for whatever `TagDevice` does (which ultimately hits the DB via `anonstore`), and there is no longer an explicit 2-minute cap. Whether it can hang “indefinitely” depends on whether `ctx` carries a deadline (not shown in the diff), so the worst-case claim isn’t fully provable, but the synchronous + removed timeout regression is verifiable and a meaningful availability/perf concern rather than a pure style issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative caching for rejected devices: the local cache entry is only set after a successful CreateOrUpdateDevice, so an over-limit device re-executes the full path (CountDevices range scan plus a doomed UPDATE) synchronously on every request, creating a load-amplification/DoS vector; known devices on cache expiry also pay 2 queries instead of 1 upsert when the limit is enabled

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds a device-limit path in `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`: when `s.deviceLimit > 0` it first calls `CountDevices(...)` and, if `count >= s.deviceLimit`, it runs `updateDevice(...)` (an `UPDATE ... WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?`) which returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `rowsAffected == 0`. This means an over-limit *unknown* device will execute at least two DB operations (count + doomed update) every time it tries to tag, and `client.go` now calls `TagDevice` synchronously and propagates `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, so repeated requests can repeatedly trigger that heavier path. However, the finding’s specific claim about the local cache only being set after a successful `CreateOrUpdateDevice` can’t be verified from the shown diff because the cache write logic isn’t included here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateDevice misinterprets RowsAffected() == 0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached: on MySQL (go-sql-driver defaults to changed rows, not matched rows, unless clientFoundRows is set), a value-identical UPDATE such as two tags of the same device within the same timestamp precision reports 0 affected rows, causing spurious 401 auth failures for legitimate already-registered devices; the same conflation fires if the row is deleted concurrently between the COUNT and the UPDATE

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the code treats `rowsAffected == 0` from the `UPDATE anon_device ...` as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. But `RowsAffected()` can be 0 even when the row matches, e.g., when the new values are identical to existing values (common behavior on MySQL depending on driver/session settings). Since the UPDATE sets `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at` to the provided values, a request that re-tags a device without changing those fields (or within timestamp precision) could incorrectly return `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which then propagates up to authentication (`client.go` returns the error), causing spurious auth failures. Also, 0 affected rows conflates “no matching row (deleted or outside time window)” with “matched but no change,” so the error mapping is unsound.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Core success path of the feature is untested: no test verifies that an existing device with updated_at inside the window is still updatable when the limit is reached (updateDevice affecting exactly 1 row and returning nil); a regression in the updated_at BETWEEN bounds would lock out every existing device while the suite stays green

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new limit/expiration logic in `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` that, once `count >= s.deviceLimit`, routes to `s.updateDevice(ctx, device)` (with an `updated_at BETWEEN ...` predicate). The only new test (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`) covers the failure path (attempting to add a *new* device when limit=1 returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`), but there is no test that exercises the success path where the limit is reached and an *existing* device is updated such that `updateDevice` affects 1 row and returns nil. This leaves the correctness of the `updated_at BETWEEN` bounds unverified by the suite, so a regression there could break updates while tests still pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anonymous.Authenticate behavioral change has zero test coverage: auth changed from a fire-and-forget goroutine (own 2-min timeout + recover()) to a synchronous TagDevice whose ErrDeviceLimitReached fails the entire authentication; no test verifies new device rejection at auth, existing device success, that non-limit TagDevice errors are logged but do not fail auth, the resulting HTTP status (raw error likely mapped to 500), or the removed panic recovery

adjudication_records.issue_text: Count-then-act race in CreateOrUpdateDevice allows exceeding the limit: CountDevices and the insert/update run with no transaction or locking between them, so two concurrent first-time devices can both observe count < limit and both insert, overshooting the cap; no test demonstrates or guards behavior under concurrent requests

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anonymous auth now synchronously blocks on DB tagging: the fire-and-forget goroutine on context.Background() with its 2-minute timeout was removed, so TagDevice runs inline in Authenticate for every cache-miss request even when device_limit=0, adding DB latency to anonymous request latency with no timeout bound — a slow or hung DB stalls anonymous auth, turning a tracking side-effect into an availability dependency for all anonymous viewers

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Anonymous.Authenticate` no longer tags the device in a background goroutine with `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)`. Instead it now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` inline and only logs errors (except `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, which is returned). adjudication_records.issue_text: MySQL changed-rows semantics can reject legitimate, already-registered devices: updateDevice interprets RowsAffected()==0 as device limit reached, but go-sql-driver's default (without clientFoundRows=true in the DSN) reports rows changed rather than matched, so an existing active device with unchanged client_ip/user_agent and same-second updated_at matches the WHERE clause but changes nothing, yielding a spurious ErrDeviceLimitReached and locking out a valid device; needs verification against the MySQL DSN and a MySQL integration test

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the code treats `RowsAffected()==0` as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. But `RowsAffected==0` can mean “matched row but no data changed” (e.g., MySQL’s default changed-rows reporting, or cases where `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at` resolve to the same stored values due to timestamp precision). In that case an already-registered device would incorrectly be rejected once the device limit is hit, even though the `WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` matched. The diff shows no additional existence check, so this can lock out legitimate devices under limit conditions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Device-limit exhaustion is a cheap, long-lived lockout: device identity is client-side-derived (cookie / IP+UA), so an attacker can mint unlimited unique device identities and fill every configured slot, after which every new legitimate anonymous device is hard-rejected for up to 30 days (slots only free on 30-day idle or login-triggered untag), with no per-source rate limiting, slot eviction, or challenge to mitigate it

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a hard “device limit” enforcement path that can deny anonymous auth when the limit is reached. In `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`, when `s.deviceLimit > 0` and `count >= s.deviceLimit`, it *never* inserts new devices and instead calls `s.updateDevice`; `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when no existing row is updated (rowsAffected==0). In `anonimpl/client.go`, `Authenticate` now returns an error immediately when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`, so new/unknown devices are hard-rejected. Because the count window is 30 days (`anonymousDeviceExpiration = 30*24*time.Hour`) and there’s no eviction strategy in this change beyond aging-out by time window, hitting the limit can lock out additional anonymous devices for a long time, making exhaustion a realistic DoS risk if an attacker can generate many distinct device IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Over-limit clients receive opaque 500s: returning the raw ErrDeviceLimitReached makes the authn chain treat it as a hard internal error rather than ErrContextAwareClientNotAuthenticated, so affected devices get generic internal-server errors indistinguishable from an outage in error-rate metrics and alerting, giving operators no signal that the configured limit is full — a dedicated error mapping/response is needed

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that when the device limit is reached, anonstore.CreateOrUpdateDevice can return the new exported sentinel `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), and `Anonymous.Authenticate` now propagates that exact error upward (`return nil, err`) instead of just logging it asynchronously (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go). However, the PR diff does not show how the authn chain / HTTP layer maps errors returned from `Authenticate` to status codes (500 vs 401/429/etc), so the specific claim that clients receive “opaque 500s” and that metrics/alerting are impacted cannot be verified from the diff alone. What is verifiable is the lack of any dedicated error mapping/translation in this change, making it a concrete design/behavior concern grounded in the diff, but not provably a correctness defect without seeing upstream error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: errors.Is sentinel matching is fragile: a %v wrap instead of %w anywhere in an intermediate layer would silently turn the device limit into a no-op (auth proceeds, logged as a warning) — worth guarding with a test

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces special handling in `anonimpl/client.go` where only `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)` causes `Authenticate` to fail; otherwise it logs a warning and proceeds. Today `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned directly from `anonstore.(*AnonDBStore).updateDevice`/`CreateOrUpdateDevice` (no wrapping shown), so there’s no verifiable bug in this diff. However, the review point is concrete and diff-grounded: if a future/intermediate layer starts wrapping the error without `%w`, the `errors.Is` check would stop matching and the limit would degrade into “warn and continue”. There’s currently no test covering the end-to-end `Authenticate` behavior under device-limit error (only a store-level test exists).
